blindSummary: Trans visitors here face one of the world's most dangerous legal environments. The 1983 penal code criminalises "acts against nature" with death by stoning (there is a de facto moratorium on executions, but the statute is live), and an independent rights-research publication documents that gender nonconformity is effectively criminalised through debauchery, heresy and religious-morality provisions — trans people can be apprehended solely for their gender expression. There is no legal gender recognition, no healthcare, no visible community, and religious courts operate alongside the civil system.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust's country profile documents that this country criminalises same-sex sexual activity with a possible death penalty under religious law.

Rights-research publication country review: gender nonconformity is effectively criminalised through 'debauchery', 'heresy' and religious-law provisions - trans people can be apprehended solely for their identity and expression; no gender-affirming healthcare; no legal recognition framework (legislation grounded in religious law precludes transition); grave lack of information on the trans community.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct punishable by death under religious-law-derived provisions; significant societal stigma; no recent executions reported.

Campaign news site (Jan 2026), based on an international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview: the penal code provides a maximum sentence of death by stoning for men; the government confirmed a de facto moratorium in 2021; arrests, detentions and harassment reported; low visibility fuels stigma; this country became a refuge for some LGBTIQ people from a neighbouring state after 2008.

A national freethinkers' association (founded 2014), describing itself as the voice of freethinkers in this country - mission to combat mistreatment and prejudice towards non-believers and LGBTQ individuals, eradicate systemic discrimination; publishes on the criminalisation law, apostasy/blasphemy laws, and the story of the first openly trans woman to appear in the country's media.
blindTangential: “Acts against nature” carries death by stoning (moratorium on executions, statute live) — a catastrophic formal exposure for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
